verses.80:2: {exsultate} Deus, {adjutori}: * aclamai ao Deus de Jacó.
verses.80:3: {sumite} um salmo, e {date}: * o saltério {jucundum} com a cítara.
verses.80:4: Tocai a trombeta {neomenia}, * no dia {insigni} da vossa solenidade.
verses.80:5: Porque é um decreto em Israel: * e um juízo {deojacob}.
verses.80:6: Em José {posuit}, quando saía da terra do Egito: * ouviu uma língua que não conhecia.
verses.80:7: {divertit} dos fardos as suas costas: * as suas mãos serviram {cophino}.
verses.80:8: Na tribulação me invocaste, e eu te livrei: * escutei-te {abscondito} da tempestade: provei-te junto à água da {contradictionis}.
verses.80:9: Ouve, meu povo, e {contestabor}: * Israel, se me ouvires, não haverá em ti um deus {recens}, nem adorarás um deus estranho.
verses.80:11: Pois eu sou o Senhor, teu Deus, que {eduxi} da terra do Egito: * {dilata} a tua boca, e eu a encherei.
verses.80:12: {et12} o meu povo não ouviu a minha voz: * e Israel não me atendeu.
verses.80:13: E eu os deixei ir segundo os desejos do seu coração: * {ibunt} suas invenções.
verses.80:14: Se o meu povo me tivesse ouvido: * se Israel tivesse andado nos meus caminhos:
verses.80:15: {pronihilo} eu teria humilhado os seus inimigos: * e teria {misissem} a minha mão sobre os que os atribulam.
verses.80:16: Os inimigos do Senhor lhe mentiram: * e o tempo deles será pelos séculos.
verses.80:17: E os alimentou {adipe}: * e da rocha os saciou de mel.

decisions.why: *exsultáre* + dative: the glossary's open row *exultar para* was made in Ps 2:11 (*exultai para ele*) and names this verse. The dative is the Greek's too (ἀγαλλιᾶσθε τῷ θεῷ). *exultar em* is *exsultáre in* (32:1 *Exultai no Senhor*) and would say where the joy rests rather than to whom it goes; a bare *Exultai a Deus* is not Portuguese (*exultar* takes no object, as the 50:16 row says).

options.label: Exultai para
options.note: Ruling: the row, as at 2:11; keeps the dative.

options.label: Exultai em
options.note: the natural Portuguese build, but it is *exsultáre in*'s (32:1).

options.label: Exultai diante de
options.note: the Ps 2 stylist's proposal; refused there as *in conspéctu*'s relation.

decisions.why: *adjútor → auxílio* (row, uniform 14/14, open for Gustavo): the person named by what he gives, as with *suscéptor → amparo*. DRB 'our helper'; MS1932 *nosso protector* (that is *protéctor*'s word).

options.label: nosso auxiliador
options.note: the agent noun; the row's standing option.

decisions.why: *súmere* is 'take up' (λάβετε ψαλμόν); DRB 'Take a psalm'. MS1932 *Entoai um salmo* gives the sense, but *entoar um salmo* is the psalter's fixed rendering of *psalmum dícere* (17:50, 56:8, 65:1, 67:5a), so using it here would make two Latin phrases one. *Tomai um salmo* keeps the Latin's verb and is heard at once as 'take up a song'.

options.label: Entoai
options.note: MS1932; collides with *psalmum dícere → entoar um salmo*.

options.label: Erguei
options.note: 'raise a psalm'; more native, but 'raise' is not *súmere*.

decisions.why: *date týmpanum* (δότε τύμπανον) is 'give the drum' — sound it, or hand it over (DRB 'bring hither the timbrel'). *Dai* keeps the Latin's verb and both readings; *tocai* (MS1932 *tocai os timbales*) decides for one. *týmpanum* → *tamborim*, the hand-drum, as 67:26 *tympanistriárum → moças que tocavam tamborins*; *tímpano* is the ear's drum or the orchestra's kettle-drum to a Brazilian. *Tocai* is also taken by *buccináte* in the next verse.

options.label: tocai o tamborim
options.note: MS1932's verb; decides the sense and repeats *Tocai* of 80:4.

options.label: trazei o tamborim
options.note: DRB 'bring hither'; decides the other way.

options.label: dai o tímpano
options.note: the cognate; heard as the eardrum.

decisions.why: *jucúndus → agradável* (open row, which names this verse; τερπνόν, 'delightful'). DRB 'pleasant'. MS1932 *harmonioso* describes the sound, which the word does not say. *suave* is kept for *suávis*.

options.label: deleitoso
options.note: closer to τερπνόν, but the row keeps it for *delectári*.

decisions.why: *Neoménia* is the Greek word for the new moon (νεομηνία), carried over by the Latin. MS1932 keeps *Neoménia*, which a Brazilian does not know. *lua nova* is the word's own meaning, not a gloss, and is plain.

options.label: na lua nova
options.note: Ruling: the meaning of the word, in plain Portuguese.

decisions.why: *insígnis* (from *signum*; Greek εὔσημος, 'well-marked') is 'marked out, distinguished'; DRB 'the noted day'. *assinalado* keeps the sign in the root and in Brazil *o dia assinalado* is the appointed day, which is what a feast is. The cognate *insigne* is correct but bookish beside *dia*, and MS1932 has it.

options.label: assinalado
options.note: Ruling: *signum* kept in the root; a living phrase.

decisions.why: *Deo Jacob* is a dative (τῷ θεῷ Ιακωβ), and the Latin leaves open whether the ordinance is the God of Jacob's (possession, as MS1932 *uma ordem do Deus de Jacob*) or is kept for him (DRB 'a judgment to the God of Jacob'). *do* reads the dative of possession, which the parallel colon *in Israël* ('a statute in Israel') points to; *para o* keeps the case but is heard as 'a judgment in favour of God'. Ruled *do*; the Latin's case is the option.

options.label: para o Deus de Jacó
options.note: the case to the letter; DRB 'to the God of Jacob'.

decisions.why: *pónere* with a predicate noun: 'he set it (the ordinance) as a testimony in Joseph'. The *pónere + predicate* row asks for the verb the Portuguese build wants; here *pôr … como* is sayable and keeps the Latin's verb. *illud* is neuter ('it' — the statute of 80:5); *o* carries it. *Em José* moves to the front, as the Latin's *in Joseph* stands early, and lets the pronoun stand before the verb. The subject is not named in the Latin; it is God by 80:5. MS1932 *Estabeleceu isto como lei para José* changes both the verb and the noun.

options.label: o pôs como testemunho
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's verb and noun.

options.label: fez disso um testemunho
options.note: the *fazer de* build of the row (17:12).

decisions.why: *divértere ab* is 'turn aside from' (L&S); the Greek ἀπέστησεν is 'removed'. *Afastou dos fardos as suas costas* keeps the image: the back taken away from under the loads. *dorsum → costas* (the human back, per the *dorsum* row; *dorso* is an animal's). The subject is God (Latin third person, against the Hebrew's first). MS1932 *Libertou os seus ombros* changes both words.

options.label: Desviou
options.note: the root of *divértere*; *desviar as costas* is odd.

options.label: Livrou
options.note: near MS1932; interprets and takes *liberáre*'s verb (80:8).

decisions.why: *cóphinus* is a basket (L&S), singular in the Latin and the Greek (ἐν τῷ κοφίνῳ). DRB 'in baskets' and MS1932 *dos cestos* put it in the plural. The hands 'served in the basket': the labourer's basket for earth and bricks. Kept singular, not explained.

options.label: no cesto
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's number and preposition.

decisions.why: *in abscóndito* + genitive → *no lugar escondido de*, as 26:5 (*no lugar escondido da sua tenda*) and 30:21 (*no lugar escondido da vossa face*). DRB 'in the secret place of tempest'; MS1932 *no recôndito* is bookish.

options.label: no segredo
options.note: shorter; moves the image from a place to a secret.

decisions.why: *contradíctio → contenda* is the open row (17:44, 30:21, 54:10), made because *contradições* was heard as inconsistencies. The row itself sets this verse and 105:32 apart: *aqua contradictiónis* is the name of a place (Meribah, 'strife'), and in a name the fault does not arise — *a água da contradição* is heard as a name. DRB 'the waters of contradiction'; MS1932 *águas da contradição*. The Latin's singular *aquam* is kept. 105:32 should copy this.

options.label: contradição
options.note: Ruling: a name, as the row foresaw; DRB, MS1932.

decisions.why: The Greek is 49:7's word for word (διαμαρτύρομαί σοι), where the Latin has *testificábor tibi* and the text reads *e eu te darei testemunho* (row *testificári*, settled D44). By D15's test (one Greek, one Portuguese), the same words here. *contestári* in L&S is 'call to witness'; DRB 'I will testify to thee'. MS1932 *eu te instruirei* interprets. The solemn warning (the sense of διαμαρτύρομαι) is carried by what follows.

options.label: eu te advertirei
options.note: the solemn warning of διαμαρτύρομαι; interprets.

decisions.why: *recens* is 'fresh, new' (πρόσφατος); DRB 'no new god', MS1932 *Deus novo*. *recente* is correct but is heard as a date. The articles *um deus … um deus* are supplied (43:21 *um deus estranho*).

decisions.latin: qui edúxi te de terra Ægýpti
decisions.why: *edúcere* is an open row: *fazer sair* where there is no *de* (17:20, 65:12), and the row foresees *tirar de* where there is (29:4 *tirastes do inferno*, 39:3 *me tirou da cova*). The Exodus formula takes *tirar*; MS1932 has the same. *te fiz sair* keeps the 'lead out' better and is the option.

*dilatáre os* is 'open the mouth wide' (πλάτυνον τὸ στόμα; DRB 'open thy mouth wide'). The same Latin phrase at 34:21 is *escancararam contra mim a sua boca* — right there, where the mouth is a mocker's; here it is a nestling's mouth held open to be filled, and *escancarar* would be heard as coarse. *Abre bem* is the idiom a Brazilian uses for exactly this; *bem* carries the *di-* of the verb. The dilatáre row is open and already has two renderings (4:2a, 118:32). Consistency with 34:21 is the option.

options.label: abre bem
options.note: Ruling: the living idiom for the Latin's sense; MS1932 *abre*.

options.label: escancara
options.note: = 34:21 for the same Latin; harsh here.

options.label: alarga
options.note: the verb to the letter (17:37 *Alargastes os meus passos*); odd with *boca*.

decisions.why: The Latin says *Et*; the turn is adversative in sense (DRB 'But'), and MS1932 keeps *E*. The psalm's chain of *et* (80:12, 13, 17) is kept as the Latin has it.

options.label: Mas
options.note: DRB 'But'; states what the Latin leaves to the hearer.

decisions.why: *ire* is 'go'; the future is kept (DRB 'they shall walk', MS1932 *irão caminhando*). *irão nas suas invenções* is not a Portuguese sentence; *andarão* is *ambuláre*'s verb, which comes in the next verse (80:14 *ambulásset → tivesse andado*), and the two Latin verbs would merge. *caminharão* is the plain verb of going on foot and stays apart. *adinvéntio → invenções* (open row, 27:4, 76:13).

options.label: caminharão
options.note: Ruling: 'go', kept apart from *ambuláre → andar* in 80:14.

decisions.why: *pro níhilo* (ἐν τῷ μηδενί, 'in no time, at no cost') and *fórsitan* (the Latin's way of rendering the Greek ἄν of a counterfactual). The *pro níhilo* row settled *por nada* at 55:8 and says this verse is another build to decide locally. *Por nada* here is heard as 'for next to nothing, at no cost' (as one buys something *por nada*), which is the sense; it keeps the Latin's word where *facilmente* (MS1932) and *em breve* (DRB 'soon') explain. *talvez* is kept because the Latin says *fórsitan*; set between commas it reads as the speaker's reserve, not as doubt about the verb.

options.label: Por nada, talvez,
options.note: Ruling: both Latin words kept; the row's *por nada*.

options.label: Por nada
options.note: *fórsitan* left to the conditional mood, as DRB and MS1932 do.

decisions.why: *míttere* is mostly *enviar* in this psalter (17:15, 17:17, 56:4); with *super* and a thing thrown it is *lançar* (21:18 *lançaram sortes*). 'Send my hand upon' is the gesture of striking (ἐπέβαλον); *lançar a mão sobre* says it, where *enviar a mão* is not Portuguese. MS1932 *descarregado* interprets.

The *adeps* row names this verse (= 147:3): 'the fat of wheat' is the finest of it, and *a flor do trigo* (MS1932) is the Portuguese idiom — but it swaps the Latin's image for another, and rule 5 names *fat* among the concrete images that stay. DRB keeps 'the fat of wheat'. *da gordura* also keeps the *ex … de* parallel with *de petra* (*da rocha*). 147:3 should copy this.

options.label: com a flor do trigo
options.note: MS1932 *da flor do trigo*; the idiom, another image.

choices.80:2: *jubiláre → aclamar* (D43); *Deo Jacob → ao Deus de Jacó* (74:10). The people are addressed as *vós* (plural humans).
choices.80:3: *psaltérium → saltério*, *cíthara → cítara* (open rows, 32:2). The verse ends on the proparoxytone *cítara*, as the Latin ends on *cíthara*.
choices.80:4: *buccináte … tuba → Tocai a trombeta*: the verb 'blow the trumpet' and its instrument are said by one Portuguese verb and its object; *tuba → trombeta* (46:6). *solemnitátis vestræ → da vossa solenidade* (73:4 *solenidade*): the Latin's *vestræ* (the Greek has 'our'), said to the people.
choices.80:5: *præcéptum → decreto* (D19; this verse is in its list). *in Israël* → *em Israel*, the Latin's preposition (the Greek has a dative). The subject of *est* (the feast of 80:4) is left unspoken, as in the Latin.
choices.80:6: *cum exíret* has no named subject: God (the Hebrew's reading) or Joseph (the people); *quando saía* keeps it open. *linguam, quam non nóverat, audívit*: the subject again unnamed; the Latin's object-first order is put in Portuguese order. *nóverat* (pluperfect of *nosco*, 'had come to know' = knew) → *não conhecia*.
choices.80:7: *ejus … ejus → as suas … as suas*: Joseph's, as the Latin.
choices.80:8: God speaks from here to the end, and speaks to Israel as *tu* (D17). *invocáre → invocar*, *liberáre → livrar*, *exaudíre → escutar* (D3), *probáre → provar* (16:3, 65:10).
choices.80:9: *Audi, pópulus meus → Ouve, meu povo*, word for word 49:7's opening. The DO verse joins the Vulgate's 9 and 10 into one prayed verse; the long second colon is the Latin's. *aliénus → estranho* (row; 43:21 *um deus estranho*).
choices.80:11: *Ego enim sum → Pois eu sou*. *Dóminus Deus tuus → o Senhor, teu Deus* (the comma for the apposition).
choices.80:13: *dimíttere* (let go) *→ deixar ir* (row, from the Nunc dimittis). *cordis eórum* singular *→ do seu coração*.
choices.80:14: The Latin's second *si* stands inside its colon (*Israël si*); Portuguese puts it first. *ambuláre → andar* (row), *via → caminho*.
choices.80:15: The counterfactual (*humiliássem … misíssem*) → *teria humilhado … teria lançado*, answering *tivesse ouvido* of 80:14. *tribulántes eos → os que os atribulam* (row *tribuláre*). The Latin order *super tribulántes … manum meam* is turned so that the colon ends on the verb phrase's natural close.
choices.80:16: *mentíri* + dative *→ mentir a* (17:46). *in sǽcula → pelos séculos* (D43; this verse is in its list). *tempus eórum* is left as open as the Latin: the enemies' time, most readers say.
choices.80:17: The speaker returns to the third person (*cibávit*), as the Latin has it, against the Hebrew. *petra → rocha* (row); definite here, *da rocha*, because it is the rock of the desert and Portuguese says *de uma rocha* only of any rock. *saturáre → saciar* (row), with *de*, as 16:14c *saciados de filhos*. *cibáre → alimentar*.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps080.md (no Diurnal text for this psalm in the parallels file). Hard readings: 80:5 the dative *Deo Jacob*; 80:6 the unnamed subjects of *exíret* and *audívit*; 80:8 *aqua contradictiónis* as a name; 80:9 *contestábor* against 49:7's *testificábor* (one Greek); 80:11 *diláta os* against 34:21; 80:15 *pro níhilo fórsitan*; 80:17 *ádipe fruménti*.

Hard checks pass. Soft: 80:4b +3 (*assinalado* is two syllables longer than *insigne*; accepted for the plain word, *insigne* is option 2); 80:8a -3 and 80:11a -4 (Portuguese is shorter; accepted); 80:15b +4 (the compound conditional *teria lançado* answering *tivesse ouvido*; accepted, within one breath). The proparoxytone close of 80:3 (*cítara*) and 80:16 (*séculos*) mirrors the Latin's. No rhyme flags.
